title: Train what happens after the flick, not only the flick itself
summary: Post-flick tasks are valuable because they force large flick speed, immediate stability, and tension control to coexist inside the same rep.
why: What happens immediately after the large flick is often the real scoring bottleneck.
The best post-flick players still flick quickly, but they release tension soon enough to stabilize or track immediately.
actions: After each large flick, pay attention to whether you can settle or track immediately without an extra wobble.
Use post-flick tasks to practice releasing tension before the landing rather than after the miss happens.
Treat the follow-up stability as part of the flick skill, not a separate afterthought.
avoid: Do not judge these tasks only by the initial flick speed.
Avoid staying tense through the landing and then trying to fix it with a second correction.

drills.label: Flick technique post flick
drills.reason: These tasks make the recovery and immediate stability after a wide flick impossible to ignore.

evidence.claim: Post-flick tasks focus on what happens after the flick and are excellent for tension control mid-flick.
evidence.excerpt: What I mean by it is flicking scenarios that focus on what happens after the flick.
